golfastr 0.3.0 is the biggest release so far: shot-level data, strokes
gained, win probability, ID crosswalks, logos and equipment. The examples
below use the 2025 Players Championship, which Rory McIlroy won in a playoff
over J.J. Spaun. The full list of changes is in the
[changelog](../news/index.html).

```{r}
library(golfastr)
library(dplyr)
```

## ShotLink: every stroke since 2012

`load_shots()` returns every stroke from PGA Tour ShotLink for 2012 to now:
distance, distance to the hole, lie before and after, and the play-by-play
text. Recent seasons also have shot coordinates and launch monitor readings
(club speed, ball speed, spin, launch angle, apex height).

```{r}
shots <- load_shots(2025, "Players")

shots |>
  filter(player_name == "Rory McIlroy", round == 1, hole == 1) |>
  select(stroke, distance, distance_remaining, from_location, to_location)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   stroke distance distance_remaining from_location to_location
#>    <int>    <dbl>              <dbl> <chr>         <chr>
#> 1      1   276                139    Tee Box       Right Fairway
#> 2      2   137                  2.39 Fairway       Left Green
#> 3      3     2.39              NA    Green         Green
```

Two more loaders come from the same feed:

* `load_tee_times()` gives pairings, tee times and the starting hole for
  every round.
* `load_course_setup()` gives par, yardage and pin position by hole and
  round.

All three read season files from GitHub releases and take a `tournament`
filter. `load_shots()` and `load_tee_times()` also take a `player` filter.

## Strokes gained for every player

`calculate_strokes_gained()` scores each shot against a baseline of expected
strokes by lie and distance, fit from ShotLink. `summarise_strokes_gained()`
adds it up by round, tournament or season (as per-round averages), adjusted
to the field.

```{r}
sg <- calculate_strokes_gained(shots)

summarise_strokes_gained(sg, by = "tournament") |>
  arrange(desc(sg_total)) |>
  select(player_name, sg_ott, sg_app, sg_arg, sg_putt, sg_total) |>
  head(5)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 6
#>   player_name    sg_ott sg_app sg_arg    sg_putt sg_total
#>   <chr>           <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>      <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 Rory McIlroy  -0.254   2.72  -0.230  1.42          3.65
#> 2 J.J. Spaun     0.395   2.62   0.641 -0.0000578     3.65
#> 3 Lucas Glover   0.516   0.567  1.26   0.814         3.15
#> 4 Tom Hoge       0.543   1.92  -0.264  0.952         3.15
#> 5 Akshay Bhatia -0.0872  1.65   0.255  1.34          3.15
```

McIlroy and Spaun tied after 72 holes, so their totals match. They got
there differently: McIlroy lost strokes off the tee and made them up on
the greens, and Spaun gained nothing putting.

Season totals track the PGA Tour's official strokes gained total closely
(correlation 0.97 in 2025 and 0.98 in 2026). They also cover every player
in the field, not only those with enough measured rounds.

## Win probability after every hole

`load_holes()` now goes back to 2004 and has four new columns:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `win_prob` | Chance of winning after the hole |
| `win_prob_before` | Chance of winning before the hole |
| `wpa` | Win probability added by the hole |
| `skill_rating` | The player's rating going into the event |

```{r}
holes <- load_holes(2025, "Players")

holes |>
  filter(player_name %in% c("Rory McIlroy", "J.J. Spaun")) |>
  arrange(desc(abs(wpa))) |>
  select(player_name, round, hole, score, win_prob, wpa) |>
  head(6)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 6
#>   player_name  round  hole score win_prob    wpa
#>   <chr>        <int> <int> <int>    <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 J.J. Spaun       5    17     6    0     -0.5
#> 2 Rory McIlroy     5    17     4    1      0.5
#> 3 Rory McIlroy     4     8     2    0.492  0.267
#> 4 J.J. Spaun       4    16     4    0.463  0.255
#> 5 Rory McIlroy     4    11     4    0.648  0.250
#> 6 Rory McIlroy     4    16     5    0.513 -0.212
```

Playoff holes come through as an extra round (round 5 here). The playoff
was a coin flip until Spaun's triple bogey on 17.

The model plays out the rest of the event from every hole. Each hole is
drawn from how the field played it that day, shifted for the player's skill
rating and for how the player has done this week and this round. Cuts and
playoffs are handled. It was fit on 2004-2019 and is calibrated on
2020-2026 events it never saw.

For an event in progress, or your own hole data, use
`add_win_probability()`:

```{r}
live <- load_holes(live = TRUE)
add_win_probability(live)
```

## Joining ESPN and PGA Tour data

Scoring data in golfastr uses ESPN IDs, and ShotLink uses PGA Tour IDs.
`load_player_ids()` and `load_event_ids()` link the two, so hole scores join
to shots and strokes gained.

```{r}
load_player_ids("Scheffler")
load_event_ids(2025)
```

## A local database

`update_db()` builds a SQLite database (or writes to any DBI connection)
from the hosted data. Every table has a `season` column, and ShotLink tables
carry both PGA Tour and ESPN IDs. Later runs add missing seasons and refresh
the latest one.

```{r}
update_db()
```

## Logos

`load_logos()` returns logo image URLs for tours, tournaments, ShotLink
courses and clubs, with PGA Tour, ESPN and ShotLink IDs to join on. Clubs
include every host of a men's or women's major, the Ryder Cup, Presidents
Cup or Solheim Cup since 1960. Only URLs are provided, not images.

```{r}
load_logos("tournament", "Players") |>
  select(name, logo_url, pga_tournament_id)
```

## What's in the bag

`load_witb()` returns player equipment, one row per club, with head, loft,
shaft and grip specs. Bags come from GolfWRX and PGA Tour Club Tracker
posts, and every row keeps its source URL. `load_witb_switches()` lists
each equipment change by slot.

```{r}
load_witb("Scheffler", slot = "driver") |>
  filter(as_of_date == max(as_of_date)) |>
  select(as_of_date, head_brand, head_model, loft_stated, shaft_model)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>   as_of_date head_brand head_model loft_stated shaft_model
#>   <date>     <chr>      <chr>            <dbl> <chr>
#> 1 2026-09-24 TaylorMade Qi4D                 8 Ventus Black 7

load_witb_switches("Scheffler", slot = "driver") |>
  select(component, old_value, new_value, first_seen_new)
#> # A tibble: 7 × 4
#>   component old_value               new_value      first_seen_new
#>   <chr>     <chr>                   <chr>          <date>
#> 1 head      G400 LST                Stealth Plus   2022-02-13
#> 2 head      Stealth Plus            Stealth 2 Plus 2023-02-12
#> 3 head      Stealth 2 Plus          Qi10           2024-03-05
#> 4 head      Qi10                    Qi4D           2025-12-09
#> 5 head      Qi4D                    Qi10           2026-01-25
#> 6 head      Qi10                    Qi4D           2026-08-16
#> 7 shaft     Atmos Black Tour Spec 7 Ventus Black 7 2022-02-13
```
